title: The Largest Opioid Review Yet: Often No Better Than Placebo
hook: The biggest review yet of opioids for short-term pain found their benefits are often small and brief — and for some surgeries and kidney stones, no better than a placebo.
key_points: Largest review to date of opioids for acute (short-term) pain.
Benefits were often small and short-lived; for some surgeries and kidney stone pain, opioids matched placebo.
Opioid users had higher rates of side effects.
Dependence can begin after only a short course — a reason to ask about alternatives.
content_html: Opioids are still routinely handed out for short-term pain — after surgery, for a kidney stone, for an injury. The largest review of that practice yet reaches an uncomfortable conclusion: the benefits are often small and short-lived, and for several common conditions, opioids worked no better than a placebo.
extra_html: The review also found opioid users had more side effects, and it echoed a now-familiar warning: physical dependence can take hold after only a short period of use. None of this means pain should go untreated — it means it's worth asking a clinician whether a non-opioid option (like acetaminophen or an anti-inflammatory) would work as well with less risk. Reported by ScienceDaily.

related.title: Using Pain Relievers Safely
related.hook: The pain relievers in your medicine cabinet are safe used right — and surprisingly risky used wrong. Knowing the two main types and their limits is the whole game.

related.title: Taking Medicines Safely
related.hook: Medicines help only when used right. Most medication mishaps are preventable with a few habits — reading the label, knowing your list, and asking questions.

related.title: Understanding Addiction
related.hook: Addiction isn't a lack of willpower or a moral failing — it's a treatable medical condition that changes how the brain works. And like other chronic illnesses, it responds to treatment.

flashcards.prompt: What did the largest review of opioids for short-term pain find?

choices.text: Benefits were often small, and sometimes no better than placebo
Opioids were clearly the most effective option for acute pain
Opioids had fewer side effects than the alternatives

flashcards.explanation_html: The review found small, short-lived benefits — and for some surgeries and kidney stone pain, no better than placebo — alongside more side effects.

flashcards.prompt: Why does 'dependence can begin after only a short period' matter for everyday patients?
flashcards.back_html: Even a brief course prescribed for acute pain carries a real risk of dependence — a reason to ask whether a non-opioid pain reliever would work just as well.

flashcards.prompt: For which kinds of pain did opioids perform no better than placebo in the review?
flashcards.back_html: Several common ones, including some surgeries and kidney stone pain.
